# Actuarial field guide to open source functions


### Ever try to build something from scratch? So much has already been built! Don’t reinvent the wheel. Here is a resource to get you up to speed.


[AI for Actuaries @Tesora.ai](https://substack.com/@aiforactuariestesoraai)


,[Federico Reyes Gomez](https://substack.com/@federicoreyesgomez)


, and[Philo Bishay](https://substack.com/@philobishay)


Sep 09, 2026


The CAS Open Source Committee has been working hard to give the actuarial community free actuarial tools. We’ve put together a field guide to promote their work.


A great deal already exists, more than most actuaries realize, and the point of the table below is to make it accessible, and condensed to one screen. This guide covers the


[CASACT GitHub org](https://github.com/casact) alongside the wider R, Python, and Julia ecosystems.


**Recent work (CAS)**


The busiest corner of the org is still reserving. In the first week of September alone,


[chainladder-python](https://github.com/casact/chainladder-python) saw eight contributors push twenty-seven commits to its main branch. Real features include a new


` Triangle.ffill()` for forward-filling along the development axis, a fix to how Cape Cod carries its fitted apriori into prediction, and open design proposals for reserve rollforward, scenario-based sensitivity, and triangle data-quality diagnostics. For a package already in daily production use across P&C, that is a lot of movement in seven days.


Pricing is where the newer activity sits.


[hardhat](https://github.com/casact/hardhat) arrived in July 2026 covering workers’ compensation retrospective and experience rating, and


[actsim](https://github.com/casact/actsim) landed the same month as a frequency-severity simulation engine that exports straight into chainladder-python triangles. They join a working set of Python tools already in the org:


[reinspy](https://github.com/casact/reinspy) for treaty structures,


[double_lift](https://github.com/casact/double_lift) for model comparison,


[PCDM](https://github.com/casact/PCDM) for a common data schema, and


[risky-router](https://github.com/casact/risky-router) , the Hacktuary Challenge winner.


Outside the CAS org, the one update worth flagging is


[lifelib](https://lifelib.io/) v0.13 (June 2026), which added a nested-projection example for Solvency II life capital. The


[CRAN Actuarial Science task view](https://cran.r-project.org/view=ActuarialScience) was also refreshed in June 2026 and remains the closest thing the profession has to an official R index.


Coding languages are color-coded: 🔵 R, 🟡 Python, 🟣 Julia/Other.


**Contributing**


The


[Open-Source Projects Working Group](https://casact.github.io/) coordinates this work and takes new participants. If you have never contributed to an open-source project,


[pull_request_tutorial](https://github.com/casact/pull_request_tutorial) exists so you can practice the mechanics on something low-stakes. The most useful contributions are usually the least glamorous: documentation, worked examples on the packages people already depend on, and issue triage.
